tender.description:
Market Notice:
This contract covers the delivery of a national programme to increase access to chess in state-funded schools across England, with a focus on expanding participation among pupils who may otherwise have limited access to structured enrichment activity.
The supplier will deliver an end-to-end package of support to schools, including the provision of chess equipment, teaching resources, and training for school staff to enable sustainable, school-led delivery. This will include the rollout of structured chess sessions, support for establishing and maintaining chess clubs, and the development of resources to ensure continuation beyond the life of the contract.
The programme will operate across approximately 350 to 450 eligible primary and secondary schools and is intended to reach a significant number of pupils nationally. Delivery will target areas of higher disadvantage and prioritise engagement with pupils eligible for Free School Meals (FSM), pupils with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND), and girls. The supplier will engage directly with schools and coordinate with relevant partners to support effective delivery.
The contract will run for an initial period of three (3) years, with an option to extend for a further one (1) year. It is intended to support educational enrichment, improve pupil engagement, and contribute to outcomes such as enhanced problem-solving skills, concentration, and confidence.

tender.title: Income Tax Self Assessment Ecosystem Data and Integration - Innovation-Led Proof of Concept
tender.description:
This is NOT a call for competition or requests to participate.
This IS notice of a planned procurement.
His Majesty's Revenue and Customs (HMRC) intends to commence a competitive procurement for the delivery of an innovation-led Proof of Concept (PoC) exploring how emerging technologies, richer transaction data and integrations across banking, payment, fintech and software ecosystems could support increased simplification and accuracy within Income Tax Self Assessment (ITSA).
The PoC will build, test and evaluate a working technical demonstrator. Its purpose is to generate evidence and learning, rather than develop a live service or commit HMRC to a specific future solution.
This work supports HMRC's Transformation Roadmap and aligns with HMRC's Strategic Approach to Third Party Software. It explores how banking, payments, fintech and software ecosystems can help customers manage their tax affairs through the products and services they already use, reducing administrative effort, improving visibility of tax obligations and helping customers get their tax right first time, while building on a thriving and innovative market.
Making Tax Digital (MTD) for Income Tax provides the digital foundations for ITSA and continues to roll out. Innovation across banking, payments, fintech and software markets presents opportunities to develop, test and better understand ecosystem approaches to support more efficient and effective tax administration that makes it simpler for customers to meet their tax responsibilities.
For many ITSA customers, software and fintech products already provide valuable automation and support, helping many customers to manage their tax affairs more efficiently. However, richer data, improved standards and greater interoperability may create opportunities to further enhance transaction categorisation and apportionment, reducing customer effort, supporting customer experience and ensuring more accurate tax outcomes.
HMRC wants to test and learn with the market how banks, payment providers, fintechs and software platforms can build on existing capabilities to deliver more integrated, accurate and customer-centred tax experiences, while supporting a thriving and innovative software ecosystem.
The central question for the PoC is: to what extent can future enhanced data, ecosystem integrations, and interventions reduce customer effort, improve customer experience and improve accuracy across more aspects of Income Tax Self Assessment?
HMRC welcomes ideas from suppliers which innovate further, building on today, and looking towards future capabilities. Suppliers are welcome to bid independently or in partnership to build, test and evaluate an end-to-end working technical demonstrator of enhanced future capabilities and integrations. Alongside SMEs, HMRC anticipates that this procurement will be suitable for participation by consortia involving banks, payment providers, fintechs and accounting software providers.
The following services are indicative and non-exhaustive:
•	provision of a sandbox or test environment;
•	creation and management of HMRC defined, persona-based synthetic transaction datasets, with sufficient complexity, realism and scale to fully test the technical demonstrator;
•	design, build and operation of a realistic working technical demonstrator showing how future ecosystem data and integrations could impact on transactions, including categorisation, apportionment, or establishment of gross and net income positions;
•	testing against agreed evaluation measures, including transaction treatment accuracy, tax calculation accuracy, and customer effort; and
•	evaluation of findings, lessons learned, and recommendations for potential future application.
Through the procurement HMRC may seek information relating to:
•	ecosystem data sources and standards available to suppliers;
•	accessibility, availability and interoperability of those data sources across accounting software providers and other ecosystem participants;
•	applicability of data sources and integrations across the ITSA population;
•	commercial, operational or legal factors affecting ecosystem sharing and interoperability;
•	the strengths and limitations of current and emerging approaches.
Through the PoC HMRC aims to:
•	generate evidence on the value of enriched ecosystem data, integrations and emerging technologies; and
•	evaluate how emerging banking, payments, fintech and software capabilities can work together to support an accurate and efficient ITSA.

tender.title: Independent Review of Public Space CCTV Provision in South Wales
tender.description:
Emma Wools, the Police and Crime Commissioner for South Wales ("the Commissioner") made a pledge in her election manifesto to perform a review of Closed-Circuit Television (CCTV) arrangements across the seven Local Authority (LAs) areas within the South Wales police area. 
CCTV plays a critical role in enhancing public safety, preventing and detecting crime and supporting community reassurance across South Wales.  It supports the delivery of South Wales Police and partnership priorities including; tackling serious violence and anti-social behaviour, protecting vulnerable people, and maintaining safe and vibrant town centres and night-time economies. 
An independent review shall be commissioned by the Commissioner to provide a comprehensive assessment of current public space CCTV provision.  The review shall consider the contribution, needs and opportunities presented by LAs, policing, community safety partners and other relevant stakeholders across the South Wales Police force area.  
The geographical area covers the seven Local Authority areas of Bridgend, Cardiff, Merthyr Tydfil, Neath Port Talbot, Rhondda Cynon Taf, Swansea and Vale of Glamorgan.
The review shall provide recommendations that ensure public space CCTV capability remains effective, sustainable, and fit for purpose in supporting crime prevention, public safety, and policing and partnership objectives, while establishing a clear blueprint for future delivery arrangements beyond May 2028, when new police governance arrangements are anticipated to be in place.

tender.title: Youth Justice Worker Level 4 Qualification
tender.description:
The Authority is awarding a contract for the provision of a Level 4 Youth Justice Worker Qualification.
The requirement is for an experienced learning provider to deliver a high-quality, accredited qualification grounded in the principles of trauma-informed practice for up to 500 learners. The provider must demonstrate a strong understanding of the needs and experiences of children in custodial environments, and be responsive to staffing structures, roles, and capability needs within Youth Justice settings and the custodial environment specifically. 
The Contract length will be six years and four months (a four month implementation period, five years of enrolments and a teach out period of one year) of accredited vocational training in trauma informed practice in Youth Justice, including both theory and effective practice (as outlined in the YJ Skills Matrix) to all frontline officers in the YCS in order to support the specialisation of the workforce. The course will be the equivalent to a Level 4 qualification. 
The course length will not exceed 12 months. Any learner extensions beyond the agreed duration should be discussed and approved by the Authority and will be provided at no additional cost per learner.  
The programme must be accessible across all three YOI sites in England (Yorkshire, Midlands and London) with flexibility to deliver face-to-face elements. 
Each cohort will consist of learners across all three sites; each face-to-face session will be located within 90 minutes travel time of one of these sites. The venue will then rotate between the three sites for each cohort. e.g. session one within 90 minutes of Feltham, session two within 90 minutes of Werrington and session three within 90 minutes of Wetherby.

tender.title: Active Fire Services 2027
tender.description:
Beyond Housing Ltd is a Housing Association who have a portfolio of approximately 15,000 properties in the North- East of England. There are three primary geographical areas in which Beyond Housings properties are located with approximately 10,000 houses located in the Redcar (North) area and a further 5,000 houses located in the Scarborough and Whitby areas (South).
The specific geographical areas, by postcode, that the active fire contract currently covers is, as follows, however these are subject to change as the stock profile of Beyond Housing expands. At this time Beyond Housing are not looking to split the contract into lots by geography, and are seeking one contractor to maintain Beyond Housing's compliance with all servicing requirements. 
Please note that a large percentage of stock is not near any main motorways. We have a mix of rural and non-rural locations in which our stock is based. Particularly between Redcar, Whitby and Scarborough areas, roads are predominantly single, with some dual carriageways. Seasonality is also a factor as traffic conditions and parking can be affected by tourism.  
Postcodes:
-	YO11,12,13,14,21,22
-	TS6,7,9,10,12,13,14
-	DL3
Contractors will be working in premises that are occupied by Beyond Housing staff, customers and members of the public. Premises consist of, but are not limited to, Office Buildings, Depots, Community Centres, extra care/supported living premises and multi-storey residential premises. 
The Active Fire contract is managed by the Facilities Team at Beyond Housing. 
This opportunity seeks to award one main contractor, with a 2nd ranked contractor for business continuity and compliance continuity purposes should the 1st ranked contractor be unable to maintain the necessary levels of compliance with the programme. 
The proposed term is five years on a three plus two basis, with break clause.
The service elements that are currently included within the active fire contract are:
•	Emergency lights servicing and maintenance 
•	Fire alarm servicing and maintenance 
•	Communal smoke alarm servicing and maintenance 
•	Fire extinguisher servicing and maintenance 
•	Sprinklers and water mist system servicing and maintenance  
•	Wet and dry risers servicing and maintenance 
•	Automatic Opening Vent servicing and maintenance
•	Fire damper servicing and maintenance 
•	Flat Door closers (automatic and swing free) servicing and maintenance 
The contract will seek to include all the servicing requirements (annual or otherwise), plus repairs following services, and any emergency calls outs and repairs relevant to active fire systems. 
Compliance with servicing dates is of upmost importance to Beyond Housing and we wish to partner with a contractor who also seeks to deliver an excellent service with 100% compliance across all servicing elements. 
Contractors will be wholly responsible for managing and co-ordinating all necessary visits/appointments to maintain compliance with the various servicing dates. Co-ordination/scheduling will not be the responsibility of Beyond Housing. 
Beyond Housing seeks a contractor with experience and expertise of managing, repairing and programming of  DRAX fire-monitoring systems. 
Beyond Housing seeks a contractor with an established Portal for real time access to documents, programmes and electronic documentation. 
Contractors will be required to be Principal Contractor under CDM. 
Contractors will be required to meet a number of KPIs - an example document can be shared upon request. 
Procurement Overview
Beyond Housing are preparing to go out to the market to procure for Active Fire Services provisionally on or around Monday 21st September 2026, with a contract start date of 1st June 2027.  The timeline allows for a 7-week mobilisation. 
The main purpose of this exercise is to engage with the market to understand how particular challenges around compliance within the active fire remit can be appropriately addressed through a tender exercise.
Beyond Housing intends to utilise an Open Tender procedure, as opposed to any existing framework route. 
Beyond Housing are also looking to understand any value adding suggestions that companies can deliver, mainly around ensuring 100% compliance across all elements of active fire, and how this can be cost effective in a contracted arrangement.
The feedback from this exercise will help:
• Inform our procurement strategy for this requirement, and
• Assist in structuring the contract terms.
This is an information gathering exercise only to help us understand what options are available and establish a market appetite. Beyond Housing will not commit to any information provided at this stage.

Suppliers wishing to participate in this Procurement should register their interest and complete the Procurement Specific Questionnaire (PSQ) on the portal by the deadline set out in this notice and the tender documents.
As part of its Stage 1 submission, each Supplier must confirm whether it wishes to participate in:
Lot 1 only
Lot 2 only
both Lot 1 and Lot 2
Suppliers will be assessed against the Conditions of Participation applicable to each Lot for which they have applied. Progression to Stage 2 will be determined separately for each Lot.
Suppliers that pass all  mandatory pass / fail questions will proceed to have their Technical Ability Scored PSQ questions evaluated and scored in line with the scoring matrix detailed in the Supplier Guidance and other tender documents.
The 6-8 highest scoring suppliers will be shortlisted and invited to participate in the next stage of the procurement process. Where two or more suppliers achieve an equal score in sixth position, all such tied suppliers will be shortlisted. Supplier ranking is determined solely by final weighted PSQ evaluation scores.
Further information is available in the tender pack.

The Supplier shall provide sourcing, booking and ticket fulfilment services for:
•	UK & International Flights
•	UK & International Rail 
•	UK & International Accommodation Venues
•	UK Coach Travel
The Supplier shall provide both on and offline booking methods that must have the ability to book the travel types stated above for self-travel or on behalf of nominated colleagues, with instantaneous confirmation.
The values provided have been estimated based on previous volumes and are therefore subject to change as the force demands for travel may increase or decrease depending on internal and external circumstances.
